summary: Tidewave Logistics: fanout heartbeat storm causing session stalls, duplicate completions, and invoice exposure - major incident & follow-up
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 ~02:07 UTC Tidewave reported a sudden increase in request latency and streaming disconnects. Investigation found a fanout heartbeat storm originating from a misrouted scheduler retry loop which caused session coordinator congestion. Symptoms included long streaming resumption times (>30s), duplicate completions for idempotent requests, and a customer-visible invoice spike due to duplicate billing records.

Impact:
- Tidewave experienced ~18 minutes of degraded streaming for 60% of requests from their us-east endpoints.
- Approximately 1.2k requests were duplicated and billed.
- Customer-facing SLOs breached; Tidewave moved to high-severity escalation and notified their finance/comms teams.

Environment:
- prod | us-east (primary servicing pool), dedicated tenant: tidewave-enterprise-01
- Affected model slices: rwkv-14b quantized variant and redwood-v2-medium fallback

Steps to reproduce (reduced replay):
1) Replay subset of Tidewave traffic with controlled fanout concurrency (simulated 800 concurrent streams).
2) Inject a scheduler ACK delay to force client retry logic to trigger multiplexed heartbeats.
3) Observe coordinator task queue growth, streaming session reconnect bursts, and duplicated completions on the serving-runtime.

Observed logs and metrics (high-level):
- scheduler: repeated job requeue logs with exponential backoff suppressed (scheduler.log lines 02:06:45 - 02:08:00).
- session-coordinator: queue_depth spike from 120 -> 4,200 in ~90s; worker CPU saturated at 92%.
- api-gateway: 5xx rate up from 0.2% -> 6.8% and connection resets per second increased 12x.
- billing: duplicate completion webhook fired for 1,235 completions (billing-service audit stream).

Immediate mitigation taken:
- 02:15 UTC: Support applied emergency circuit-breaker rule to Tidewave tenant to limit parallel streams to 200.
- 02:22 UTC: Engineers pushed a scheduler patch to stop re-enqueueing heartbeats when coordinator backlog > 1,000.
- 02:30 UTC: Billing team paused duplicate-completion ingestion and began deduplication job on the outstanding invoices.

Current status and resolution summary:
- Root cause: scheduler retry logic failed to respect a new coordinator backpressure header introduced three weeks prior. A regression in scheduler task throttling allowed fanout heartbeats to escalate under high latency conditions, creating a positive feedback loop.
- Fix deployed: scheduler throttling conservative fallback (PR linked) and session-coordinator hard quota enforcement.
- Billing fix: retroactive dedupe job applied to outstanding invoices; customer credits calculated and applied for duplicated charges.

Notes on detection and monitoring gaps:
- Alerting thresholds did not consider combined queue_depth + heartbeat rate; only queue_depth had an alert. Heartbeat rate spikes were visible in metrics but not alerted.
- No synthetic replay detected the pattern because synthetic load used lower stream concurrency than Tidewave's production profile.

Required follow-ups (see action_items):
comments: 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC | Tidewave IT (Alex R.) - initial report: customers seeing streaming timeouts and duplicate responses; attached sample request IDs. Asked for ETA and immediate mitigation.

2026-03-10 02:18 UTC | Support (Maya Chen) - triage: escalated to SRE, applied tenant-level parallelism cap as short-term mitigation. Notified billing to hold ingestion of completion events for the tenant.
2026-03-10 02:25 UTC | SRE (Ravi Patel) - investigation note: observed scheduler requeue storm and session coordinator queue spike; rolling patch to throttle requeues underway (PR: runtime#4582).
2026-03-10 03:05 UTC | Billing (Lena Ortiz) - note: paused ingestion pipeline for tidewave-enterprise-01; starting dedupe scan. Initial estimate: ~1.2k duplicate events; preparing credit batch.

2026-03-10 08:14 UTC | Support (Maya Chen) - customer update sent: summarized mitigations, promised post-incident report and invoice credits. Customer acknowledged and requested timeline for permanent fixes.

2026-03-11 10:02 UTC | Engineering (Carlos Mendes) - follow-up: root cause confirmed; scheduler regression introduced in PR#4478 (task-throttling refactor). Patch merged and staged to prod; coordinator quotas added as defense-in-depth.

2026-03-12 16:22 UTC | Customer Success (Elena Karpova) - verified invoice credits applied and Tidewave finance confirmed receipt. Customer requested a follow-up postmortem and changes to SLA terms for high-concurrency streaming workloads.
investigation_notes: Found scheduler change 2026-02-15 removed coordinator backpressure header propagation in the refactor. This allowed scheduler to continue requeuing when coordinator was saturated.
Reproduction succeeded with synthetic replays at 750-1k concurrent streams when ACK delays > 300ms.
Session-coordinator lacked an absolute hard-cap; queue growth overwhelmed worker pools which in turn increased ACK latency creating a feedback loop.
Billing duplicates traced to webhook fanout retries; dedupe key missing request_id in some older fallback paths which allowed duplicate invoice records to be persisted.
resolution: Immediate: tenant stream cap and scheduler patch stopped the heartbeat amplification. Billing dedupe job removed duplicate invoice records and credits were applied. Long-term: added coordinator hard quota, restored backpressure header propagation, added heartbeat-rate alerting, and expanded synthetic load tests to include high-concurrency streams. Customer received credits and a compensation plan for SLA exposure.
action_items: ENG-1: Restore backpressure header propagation in scheduler and add unit + integration tests (owner: Carlos Mendes) - due 2026-03-20
SRE-1: Implement session-coordinator hard quota enforcement and autoscaling guardrails (owner: Ravi Patel) - due 2026-03-18
OBS-1: Add composite alert for queue_depth AND heartbeat_rate for all tenants (owner: Priya Shah) - due 2026-03-16
QA-1: Add high-concurrency synthetic workload (>=800 concurrent streams) to regression suite (owner: QA team) - due 2026-03-22
BILL-1: Audit billing ingestion fallback paths to ensure dedupe keys always include request_id (owner: Lena Ortiz) - due 2026-03-19
CS-1: Draft updated SLA appendix for high-concurrency streaming customers and review with Legal (owner: Elena Karpova) - due 2026-04-01
customer_communication_summary: Initial acknowledgment within 8 minutes; emergency mitigation applied within 15 minutes. Customer received detailed incident timeline and confirmation of billing credit within 24 hours. Follow-up call scheduled for 2026-03-15 to review postmortem and SLA appendix. Customer indicated acceptance of credits but requested stronger guardrails for their peak concurrency profile.
